purpose: Dronedarone is used to help keep your heart beating in a normal, steady rhythm if you have a condition called atrial fibrillation (AFib) or atrial flutter. It helps reduce how often your heart goes back into an abnormal rhythm. It also helps lower your risk of needing to go to the hospital due to heart rhythm problems.
how_it_works: Your heart uses electrical signals to keep a steady beat. In AFib, those signals become chaotic and cause an irregular heartbeat. Dronedarone works by calming down these electrical signals in the heart, helping it stay in a normal rhythm. Think of it like a traffic controller that keeps the electrical impulses in your heart moving in an orderly way.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, and feeling tired. Some people notice slow heartbeat or dizziness. Skin reactions like rash or sensitivity to sunlight can also occur. These are usually mild, but let your doctor or pharmacist know if they bother you.
warnings: This medication should NOT be used if you have severe heart failure or a condition called permanent AFib (where your heart is always in an abnormal rhythm). It can cause serious liver problems — contact your doctor right away if you notice yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, or unusual fatigue. It can also affect your lungs and kidneys, so regular check-ups are important. Tell your doctor about all other medications you take, as dronedarone interacts with many drugs including blood thinners and certain antibiotics.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one 400 mg tablet taken twice a day — once with your morning meal and once with your evening meal. Taking it with food helps your body absorb it better and may reduce stomach upset. Always take it exactly as prescribed and do not stop without talking to your doctor first.
